# QR test vectors

`qr-vectors.json` holds the expected Retail ID QR encoding and decoding results shared by the SDK test suites.

**JavaScript is the canonical implementation.** Every expected value was generated by the JavaScript SDK and is committed as a fixed value. Tests read the file and never regenerate it, so an encoder regression fails a test instead of silently updating the expectations.

Today only the JavaScript tests (`javascript/test/browser.test.ts`) consume this file. The other SDKs are expected to validate against it in follow-up changes.

## Regenerating

Only regenerate on purpose, then review the diff:

```bash
cd javascript
npm run build
node scripts/generate-qr-vectors.mjs           # write test-vectors/qr-vectors.json
node scripts/generate-qr-vectors.mjs --check   # report whether the committed file is current (writes nothing)
```

The output is deterministic and contains no timestamps or machine-specific values.

## Using it from another SDK

The `conventions` object inside the JSON is the authoritative description. In short:

- Build full URLs from `defaultDomain` (`1a4.com`): Base36 is `HTTPS://1A4.COM/<base36Code>`, Base64 is `https://1a4.com/<base64Code>`. The host never affects decoding, and a bare short code is also accepted.
- `batchId` is lowercase hex. Compare it case-insensitively, since some SDKs render uppercase.
- Every entry in `labels` must encode to exactly its two codes, and each form must decode to its `batchId` and `index` in both default and strict mode.
- `strictRejections` must be rejected in strict mode. `invalidInputs` must be rejected in both modes. Only the rejection is specified, not the error type or message.
- `customDomain` lists exact URLs for a non-default domain.
- `conventions.intentionallyExcluded` lists behavior that is deliberately not covered yet.
